name: DaisyRec 2.0
description: Recently, one critical issue looms large in the field of recommender systems -- there are no effective benchmarks for rigorous evaluation -- which consequently leads to unreproducible evaluation and unfair comparison. We, therefore, conduct studies from the perspectives of practical theory and experiments, aiming at benchmarking recommendation for rigorous evaluation. Regarding the theoretical study, a series of hyper-factors affecting recommendation performance throughout the whole evaluation chain are systematically summarized and analyzed via an exhaustive review on 141 papers published at eight top-tier conferences within 2017-2020. We then classify them into model-independent and model-dependent hyper-factors, and different modes of rigorous evaluation are defined and discussed in-depth accordingly. For the experimental study, we release DaisyRec 2.0 library by integrating these hyper-factors to perform rigorous evaluation, whereby a holistic empirical study is conducted to unveil
evaluation_method: ranking metrics such as Recall@K, NDCG@K, MRR, and HR@K
reputation: Known as a rigorous recommendation evaluation library/benchmarking framework rather than a single fixed dataset, with growing use in recommender-systems research.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; focuses on evaluation protocol rigor and hyper-factor sensitivity across datasets/models. Results depend heavily on dataset splits, negative sampling, and metric choice.
